requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate on a loop-backed PV, mkfs.ext4, and mount at /srv/data directly observed with df showing the LV mounted; fstab entry added for persistence. Loop-backed PVs were a reasonable substitute given the disk had no spare partition/free space.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: vgextend + lvextend +1100M followed by online resize2fs executed with the filesystem still mounted (no unmount step in the command sequence, confirmed by 'on-line resizing required' message and mount output showing /srv/data still mounted afterward). Final LV size 2.05 GiB (>= 2GB), also reconfirmed in the final post-restart check.

requirements.requirement: Contents stay intact through the growth operation
requirements.summary: sha256sum checksums recorded before growth and re-verified immediately after resize2fs both report OK for testfile.txt and rand.bin, directly showing no data loss during the online grow.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task - an LV mounted at /srv/data, online growth to >=2GB while mounted, and intact contents - are directly and clearly evidenced by command output (creation, online resize2fs while still mounted, and matching sha256 checksums before/after). The independently-mandated node-restart evidence protocol for node1 is also well satisfied: pre-restart boot id and health, restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot id (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and full recovery of LVM stack, mount, and data integrity, including a successful post-reboot write. Getting there required three failed reboot cycles due to real boot-ordering bugs in the executor's own auto-mount script, which were diagnosed and fixed; the underlying task data was never permanently lost, only temporarily inaccessible during self-inflicted, self-repaired filesystem corruption.
limitations: The public task did not require the LV to survive a reboot; the multi-restart debugging narrative is supplemental evidence from the separately mandated node-restart protocol, not proof required by the task instruction itself, though it does not detract from task satisfaction.

The final /srv/data mount depends on two loop-devices backed by files under /var/lib/lvm-backing rather than a raw block device/partition, a substitution driven by lack of spare disk space on vda; this is a reasonable implementation but differs from a conventional LVM-on-block-device setup.
Leftover reboot/apk log files in /tmp were not cleaned up, though they are inert and low-risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to provisioning, growing, or to diagnosing/fixing boot-order bugs uncovered by the mandatory restart protocol (which is outside the public task's scope but required by the separate node-restart evidence protocol). The first restart (cmd-5dd2a0a335b64c26) exposed a genuine defect in the executor's own boot-time loop-attach script, corrupting the ext4 superblock (observed via dmesg/e2fsck in cmd-77dac43f171c4b38); this was a bounded, low-risk mutation (loop-backed test data, not production data) that was fully repaired via e2fsck and reattachment (cmd-68042428c7af4c0f) with checksums re-verified OK. A second and third iteration of the init script were needed before the ordering bug was actually fixed (cmd-9e983089f66b4920, cmd-3857aaa1ab834ec7, cmd-b914e24b962f48bd) - each iteration is a corrective action tied to getting the mandated restart cycle to succeed cleanly, not an unrelated experiment, so these are not unnecessary mutations. The only residue left behind is a handful of leftover log files (/tmp/apk_install.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/reboot2.log, /tmp/reboot3.log, /tmp/reboot4.log) visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; these are harmless diagnostic artifacts but were never cleaned up.
